objective: Integrate the accepted verifier into the four-cell CI workflow and synchronize English, Chinese, fixture, and changelog documentation within the approved integrity claim boundary.
deliverable: A portable four-cell CI workflow and synchronized bilingual/public documentation in exactly five owned files.

authoritative_facts: CI must use exactly ubuntu-latest and windows-latest with Python 3.10 and 3.11.
Workflow permissions remain exactly contents: read and no dependency-install or network step is added.
All run commands must work in the default shell of both runner OS families.
Public claims must describe integrity or tamper detection only relative to a trusted manifest.
Strict evidence closure, crash recovery, signatures, authenticity, third-party OpenAPI semantics, and the second domain remain deferred.
accepted_upstream_results: V4-T3@2 compatibility and local-runtime verification receipt.
user_constraints: Do not add dependencies, modify historical evidence, use networked install steps, push, tag, or publish.
permissions: Edit only the five declared public integration files and run read-only checks.
non_goals: Do not change production verifier behavior or tests, create v0.4 package evidence, claim GitHub Actions passed before an authorized push, or broaden v0.4 scope.

acceptance_checks: Set the workflow matrix to the exact approved OS and Python values while retaining contents: read and bounded timeout behavior.
Run the full test suite plus separate v0.2/v0.3 structural and integrity commands in every matrix job using portable Python commands.
Remove direct GNU sha256sum reliance without adding an install or dependency step.
Synchronize version, command, test count, supported matrix, trusted-manifest premise, and deferred limitations across English and Chinese documentation.
Resolve every changed relative Markdown link and pass git diff --check for owned files.
